title: Algorithms and Big-O
targetPerformance: Within 20 focused hours, solve at least 18 of these 22 Python prompts in 30-minute timed rounds, with at least 80% first-try success; implement the core patterns from memory, state time and space complexity, and name edge cases before coding.
whyItMatters: Algorithmic patterns turn a vague problem into a small set of testable choices: how to scan, search, store, traverse, and order data. Big-O lets you predict whether a solution will still work when the input grows.

subskills.title: Read complexity from loops
subskills.why: Estimate growth before coding so a correct-looking solution does not collapse on large input.
subskills.selfCorrection: Name the input size, count how many times each loop can run, and ask whether loops are sequential or nested.
drills: Classify one-pass and nested-loop snippets.
Compare constant, logarithmic, linear, and quadratic growth.
State the extra space used by a helper data structure.

subskills.title: Shrink and advance two pointers
subskills.why: Turn many pair and boundary scans into linear passes with a visible invariant.
subskills.selfCorrection: Write what the left and right pointers still rule out after every move; test empty, singleton, duplicate, and already-sorted inputs.
drills: Check a palindrome from both ends.
Merge two sorted sequences without rereading either side.
Compact a sorted array in place and return its new length.

subskills.title: Maintain a binary-search window
subskills.why: Cut ordered search space in half instead of scanning every candidate.
subskills.selfCorrection: State what every index outside [left, right] cannot be, then verify progress when the interval has one or two items.
drills: Find the first occurrence of a duplicate target.
Return an insertion point before, between, and after values.
Trace the interval on a target that is absent.

subskills.title: Use hash maps for constant-time lookups
subskills.why: Trade predictable extra memory for fast complements, counts, and grouping.
subskills.selfCorrection: Define the key and value before the loop, and check whether the current item may reuse itself.
drills: Find two indices that sum to a target.
Locate the first non-repeating character.
Group words by a canonical anagram key.

subskills.title: Choose LIFO or FIFO state
subskills.why: Model nested delimiters, waiting work, and monotonic next-event queries with the right frontier structure.
subskills.selfCorrection: Say whether the newest or oldest pending item must be processed, then test an empty structure and a repeated value.
drills: Validate brackets while ignoring ordinary text.
Use a monotonic stack for next greater values.
Describe why a queue avoids revisiting already-served work.

subskills.title: Order data with a deliberate cost
subskills.why: Use ordering to simplify later decisions and understand the time and stability trade-offs.
subskills.selfCorrection: Write the sort key and tie-break rule explicitly; check empty input, duplicate keys, and whether the input must stay unchanged.
drills: Trace merge sort's split and merge phases.
Compare O(n log n) sorting with a linear counting pass.
Select the most frequent values with a deterministic tie-break.

subskills.title: Traverse graphs with BFS and DFS
subskills.why: Turn networks and dependencies into systematic visits while handling cycles, disconnected nodes, and start/target boundaries.
subskills.selfCorrection: Mark a node when it is discovered, not only when it is removed from the frontier, and test a cycle plus a disconnected component.
drills: Find an unweighted shortest path with BFS.
Count connected components with DFS.
State O(V+E) for adjacency-list traversal.

barriers.barrier: Big-O feels like notation without a concrete meaning
barriers.fix: Double a toy input, count the work again, and write the observed growth before naming the class.

barriers.barrier: Edge cases are postponed until after the main algorithm
barriers.fix: Make an empty, singleton, duplicate, and boundary-value table before writing the loop.

barriers.barrier: Pattern names are memorized without invariants
barriers.fix: Before coding, state what the pointers, map, stack, or frontier guarantee after each iteration.
